output.summary: A large banyan-type fig tree native to eastern South and Southeast Asia, it develops aerial and buttressing roots and broad, shiny oval leaves. In parts of India, its roots are guided across gaps to form living bridges. Young leaf tips can be eaten as salad greens, while its milky latex is toxic if swallowed.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaf tips are used as salad greens; the milky latex is toxic if ingested, and the small figs are barely edible.
